result.topic_en: Euler tabulates the residues of the squares modulo the primes 5, 13, 17, 29, 37 of the form 4n+1, then lists sums of two squares divisible by 5, 13, 17 and 29 together with their quotients.
result.transcription:
PER NVMEROS PRIMOS. 115
elicere queamus, residua ex quadratis orta pro simplicioribus apponamus:
num. primi formae $4n+1$ | Quadrata
| $1,4,9,16,25,36,49,64,81,100,121,144,169,196,225,256$ etc.
| Residua
$5$ | $1,-1,-1,1,0$
$13$ | $1,4,-4,3,-1,-3,-3,-1,3,-4,4,1,0$
$17$ | $1,4.-8,-1,8,2,-2,-4,-4,-2,2,8,-1,-8,4,1$
$29$ | $1,4,9,-13,-4,7,-9,6,-6,13,5,-1,-5,-7,-7,-5$
$37$ | $1,4,9,16,-12,-1,12,-10,7,-11,10,-4,-16,11,3,-3,-7,-9,-9.$
Hinc pro his diuisoribus formae $4n+1$ sequentes habebimus binorum quadratorum summas per eos diuisibiles:
Diuisor $5 \ldots\ldots 1$
$\frac{4}{5}$ quotus $1$.
Diuisor $13 \ldots\ldots$ $\begin{array}{r|r|r} 1 & 4 & 16 \\ 25 & 9 & 36 \end{array}$
summa $\begin{array}{r|r|r} 26 & 13 & 52 \end{array}$
quotus $\begin{array}{r|r|r} 2 & 1 & 4 \end{array}$
Diuisor $17 \ldots$ $\begin{array}{r|r|r|r} 1 & 4 & 9 & 36 \\ 16 & 64 & 25 & 49 \end{array}$
summa $\begin{array}{r|r|r|r} 17 & 68 & 34 & 85 \end{array}$
quotus $\begin{array}{r|r|r|r} 1 & 4 & 2 & 5 \end{array}$
Diuisor $29 \ldots$ $\begin{array}{r|r|r|r|r|r|r} 1 & 4 & 9 & 16 & 36 & 64 & 121 \\ 144 & 25 & 49 & 100 & 196 & 81 & 169 \end{array}$
summa .. $\begin{array}{r|r|r|r|r|r|r} 145 & 29 & 58 & 116 & 232 & 145 & 290 \end{array}$
quotus $\begin{array}{r|r|r|r|r|r|r} 5 & 1 & 2 & 4 & 8 & 5 & 10 \end{array}$
P 2 Diui-
